bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in xpath.c: xmlXPathNodeSetAdd (invoked via xmlXPathGetElementsByIds/xmlXPathIdFunction during XPath/XPointer evaluation) can access a node/attribute that was already freed while processing input (e.g. via xmlTextReader/XInclude). This results in reads of freed heap memory, leading to crashes and potential memory corruption when resolving ID-based references.
bug_description.normalized: During streaming reader cleanup, libxml2 frees an earlier element carrying xml:id while leaving its xml:id attribute registered in doc->ids if the document has no DTD subset. A later xi:include href="#a" evaluates XPointer id() against that stale ID-table entry, reloads the freed attribute, derives its freed parent element, and dereferences that freed element in xmlXPathNodeSetAdd.

source.description: Parsing the attacker-controlled xml:id attribute registers that live xmlAttrPtr in the document ID table for later id() lookups.
source.value_from: The staged PoC's main XML entity contains `<m xml:id="a"/>`; xmlSAX2StartElementNs parses that attribute and passes its value and xmlAttrPtr into xmlAddID.
source.note: This is the first project statement that creates vulnerability-relevant state: the xml:id value `a` is accepted without any DTD requirement and stored in `doc->ids` as an entry whose `id->attr` points at the live attribute node.

sink.description: The freed element pointer recovered from the stale ID lookup is dereferenced when xmlXPathNodeSetAdd reads its type.
sink.note: ASan's crashing read is the `val->type` access. In this sample `val` is the freed `<m>` element obtained from `attr->parent` after reloading a stale xml:id attribute from `doc->ids`.

root_cause.description: Streaming attribute cleanup only removes IDs when a DTD subset exists, even though xml:id attributes were registered in doc->ids without any DTD.
root_cause.note: For the PoC document there is no internal or external subset, so this guard is false and the cleanup path never calls `xmlTextReaderRemoveID(cur->parent->doc, cur)` for the xml:id attribute registered at step 1.

tainted_value_origin.note: The libFuzzer input is decoded into fuzz string pairs; the first entity pair yields the main XML entity string that contains both `<m xml:id="a"/>` and `<xi:include href="#a"/>`.

parser_admitted.code: if ((reader->xinclude) && (reader->node != NULL) && (reader->node->type == XML_ELEMENT_NODE) && (reader->node->ns != NULL) && ((xmlStrEqual(reader->node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_NS)) || (xmlStrEqual(reader->node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_OLD_NS)))) {
parser_admitted.description: The current streamed node is admitted to the XInclude/XPointer path only when it is an element in the XInclude namespace and XInclude processing is enabled.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz target decodes the staged binary input into a main XML entity and drives xmlTextReaderRead with parser options that enable XInclude processing.
Streaming parse of `<m xml:id="a"/>` registers the xml:id attribute in `doc->ids` for later XPath/XPointer id() resolution.

When the reader advances to the later `xi:include` element, it frees the previous `<m>` subtree; xmlTextReaderFreeProp skips ID-table cleanup because the document has no DTD subset, leaving a dangling xml:id entry in `doc->ids`.
XInclude evaluates the `#a` fragment through XPointer, which dispatches to XPath id() lookup on the current document.
The stale ID-table entry is reloaded as a freed attribute, converted to its freed parent element, and then dereferenced in xmlXPathNodeSetAdd.

fine_trace.note: While parsing the PoC's `<m xml:id="a"/>`, the special xml:id path registers the attribute node `ret` in `doc->ids` under the attacker-chosen value `a`. The stored entry keeps `id->attr = ret` for later `xmlGetID` lookups.
After the reader advances from `<m>` to the following `<xi:include>` sibling, streaming cleanup selects the previous `<m>` node as `tmp` and recursively frees that subtree.
Cleanup reaches the xml:id attribute as `cur`, but the no-DTD PoC document makes this guard false. `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` is therefore skipped even though step 1 already placed `cur` in `doc->ids`.

The xml:id attribute lifetime ends as property cleanup frees the attribute object, but because step 3 skipped ID removal the document ID table still retains `id->attr = cur`. The enclosing `<m>` subtree is being retired by the same recursive cleanup, so the stale attribute's `parent` will no longer point to a live element either.

Once the current streamed node is the PoC's `xi:include` element in the XInclude namespace, the reader enters XInclude processing on that node after the earlier xml:id-bearing subtree has already been retired.
XInclude evaluates the fragment string derived from `href="#a"`. The attacker-controlled identifier `a` is now the XPointer expression that will be resolved against the current document.
For a bare-name XPointer, the fragment name is pushed as a string and dispatched to XPath id() resolution, turning the attacker-controlled name `a` into an ID-table lookup request.
The ID lookup returns the stored attribute pointer from `doc->ids`. Because step 4 left the table entry stale, this returned `id->attr` is the freed xml:id attribute rather than a live node.

xmlXPathGetElementsByIds treats the stale pointer as an attribute node and reloads `elem` from `attr->parent`. That converts the freed attribute into a dangling pointer to the freed `<m>` element, which is then passed onward to nodeset insertion.
Nodeset insertion dereferences the dangling element pointer as `val` by reading `val->type`. This is the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read reported in the staged crash trace.

poc.trigger: The staged 93-byte PoC starts with the little-endian options word `0x2020ff20`, then fuzz string pairs where the main entity string is `<c xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude">><m xml:id="a"/><xi:include href="#a"/> <`. That document has no DTD, defines xml:id `a` on an earlier element, and later resolves `#a` through an XInclude/XPointer lookup after the reader has already cleaned up the earlier subtree.

format.name: libxml2-fuzz-xml-entity-pairs
format.contract: The input format is a 4-byte little-endian parser-options word followed by backslash-newline terminated fuzz strings consumed as URL/entity pairs by `xmlFuzzReadEntities`; the first pair becomes the main XML document. For this bug, the main entity must be a no-DTD XML document that places `xml:id="a"` on an earlier element and later contains an XInclude element with `href="#a"`, so reader-side subtree cleanup leaves `doc->ids` stale before XPointer id() resolves that same ID.
